newsitem.title: USA: Retail gasoline price dips slightly in February.
newsitem.headline: Retail gasoline price dips slightly in February.

text.p: U.S. retail gasoline prices dipped a modest 0.1 cent per gallon in February, the first decline in five months, the American Automobile Association (AAA) said Tuesday.
The average price of self-service regular unleaded gasoline was $1.287 per gallon, according to the survey conducted for AAA from Friday to Sunday.
The average price sat 15.8 cents above AAA's year-ago level. Retail prices had moved higher from September through December and remained steady in January.
The drop was due largely to the increase in U.S. gasoline stocks seen in recent weeks as well as typically weak February driving demand, according to AAA spokesman Mike Morrissey.

U.S. gasoline inventories have jumped nearly 13.5 million barrels in the past three weeks to sit at 207.6 million barrels, according to the latest figures released by the industry group American Petroleum Institute.
However, gasoline stocks still remain nearly 3.5 million barrels below year-ago levels, which helped trigger a sharp rally in prices at the pump ahead of 1996's summer driving season.
Average per gallon retail prices surged 17.8 cents from March through May last year, Morrissey said.
"It's difficult to say where they will go from here," he said. "But we do need to build stocks if we're going to avoid the type of price jump we saw last year."
West Coast gasoline prices were the highest in the February survey at $1.366 per gallon, up 1.8 cents from January's survey and 13.7 cents from 1996 levels.

Southeast prices sat at $1.215 per gallon, down 0.3 cent from the previous month, while the average price in New England fell 1.8 cents per gallon to $1.327. The Mid-Atlantic region saw a dip of 1 cent from January to $1.311 per gallon, the Great Lakes price fell 1.6 cents to $1.263 per gallon, Midwest prices fell 0.4 cent to $1.266 a gallon and Southwest prices gained 2.3 cents to $1.26 a gallon.

The national average price for mid-grade unleaded gasoline fell 0.5 cent from a month ago to sit at $1.366, up 14.2 cents in the year. Self-service premium was $1.436, down 0.3 cent for the month, but was up 12.9 cents from February 1996.
AAA's figures are based on data from the Oil Price Information Service in Bethesda, Md.
AAA is a nonprofit federation of 99 motor clubs and 39 million members in the United States and Canada.
